title: Meta misses earnings forecasts after Zuckerberg media push to promote AI
excerpt: Stock tumbles nearly 8% after weaker-than-expected results, despite CEO’s blitz to tout positive effects of AI
content_html:
Mark Zuckerberg’s media spree touting the positive effects of artificial intelligence did little to cushion the blow of Meta’s second-quarter earnings, which sent its stock tumbling on Wednesday.

In a Wall Street Journal op-ed published on Tuesday, the Meta chief executive expressed his optimism for a world where everyone has access to a super-intelligent machine.

“As a thought experiment, imagine only one person had a super-intelligent lawyer,” Zuckerberg wrote. “He would have an unfair advantage in court. That would lead to a worse society. But now imagine everyone has a super-intelligent lawyer. Justice would be carried out much more fairly and efficiently than it is today.”

But Zuckerberg’s message of AI optimism wasn’t enough to alleviate Wall Street’s initial reaction to Meta’s second-quarter earnings. The company’s stock slid nearly 8% after reporting weaker-than-expected results.

Meta posted $6.18 in earnings per share, missing Wall Street expectations of $7.14, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. Revenue was $60.8bn, beating analyst predictions of $60.23bn.

The company also raised the lower end of its expected expenses and spending for the year. Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, said the company had $2.4bn in “charges related to legal proceedings” in the second quarter, raising total expenses to the range of $165bn to $169bn, up from $162bn to $169bn.

And it expects 2026 capital expenditures to range from $130bn to $145bn, up from $125bn to $145bn. Meta has previously said a big portion of its capex is earmarked for its AI investments.

Zuckerberg’s PR blitz comes as investors and analysts look for the company’s justification of its massive spending on AI infrastructure, a concern that has contributed to the 10% drop in the company’s share price year over year.

Big tech companies such as Meta, which have increasingly burned through free cash flow, need to sell consumers and Wall Street on the promise of AI to defend their spending. The stock market’s response to Zuckerberg’s remarks on the company’s earnings call, scheduled for later this evening, could reveal whether his messaging is enough to ease investor concerns.

Meta has struggled to make an AI model to rival OpenAI or Anthropic, but it plans to start a cloud business to sell AI compute, monetizing some of its immense AI investments, Bloomberg reported this month. The report was one of the few things to boost investor confidence this year, spurring a spike in the stock’s long decline.

The day before earnings, Zuckerberg echoed his belief in decentralizing AI and creating an era of “personalized super-intelligence” where everyone has an AI assistant tailored to their needs and beliefs, in interviews with the New York Times and the Financial Times.

Though he did not specify how Meta plans to approach this, based on the company’s history, personalization would likely require consumers to hand over even more of their data. Still, Zuckerberg said it was better than his competitors’ centralized models.

“I think it is literally impossible to have a single benevolent super-intelligence that is simultaneously aligned with everyone at once,” Zuckerberg told the New York Times.

Meta may be “trying to do too much at once”, Mike Proulx, vice-president and research director at advisory firm Forrester Research, said.

“Every one of Meta’s major growth lanes now carries a trust toll,” Proulx said in a statement before listing Meta’s new projects. “AI-generated advertising raises new brand-control concerns, smart glasses create new privacy questions, youth safety remains under intense scrutiny and employee-tracking initiatives spark data-collection backlash.”

Zuckerberg’s narrative speaks to Meta’s need to set itself apart from competitors – many of whom he said are sending messages filled with “doom” about the future of AI.

“I don’t understand why anyone who believes that AI will eliminate most jobs and much of humanity’s relevance would rush to build that future,” Zuckerberg wrote in the WSJ.

Still, Meta’s attempt to create a positive message around its AI systems may fall flat, said eMarketer senior analyst Minda Smiley.

“It’s not surprising that Zuckerberg wants to come out with a more cohesive message around the company’s AI ambitions, especially as Meta tries to carve out its own lane,” Smiley said in a statement.

“But the optimistic, positive tone he’s striking stands in stark contrast to the negative sentiment that’s building toward social media companies over claims that they’ve harmed and addicted kids. This juxtaposition could make it more difficult for Meta to build credibility in an area where it’s already a laggard.”

While Zuckerberg makes an argument for Meta’s open-source approach to AI development, the company is being forced to answer for its previous practices developing its products and the effects they have had on users.

Meta is facing about 3,000 lawsuits alleging that it deliberately creates addictive products leading to the harm of children. The suits have been brought by families, school districts and states’ attorneys general. Forty-two states have sued Meta in state courts, with Tennessee’s case currently at trial. A separate federal lawsuit brought by 29 attorneys general goes to trial in California next month.

“The shifting regulatory environment is also a major Meta risk,” said Proulx. “Policymakers are more focused on youth wellbeing, addiction and platform safety … Youth restrictions will affect who Meta can reach. That’s a big problem for a company that depends on ad revenue.”

The lawsuits not only call Meta’s corporate practices into question; they also come at a financial cost. The company has already suffered damaging losses, with two separate juries finding Meta liable for harming children and awarding plaintiffs millions in damages. Lawyers for the families, schools and lawmakers say they will not stop seeking high-cost damages until Meta changes the design of its products.

Dara Kerr and Nick Robins-Early contributed reporting

blocks.html_en: The lawsuits not only call Meta’s corporate practices into question; they also come at a financial cost. The company has already suffered damaging losses, with two separate juries finding Meta liable for harming children and awarding plaintiffs millions in damages. content_html_zh:
马克·扎克伯格在媒体上大肆宣扬人工智能的积极影响，但并没有缓解 Meta 第二季度盈利的打击，导致其股价周三暴跌。

在周二发表的《华尔街日报》专栏中，Meta 首席执行官表达了他对每个人都可以使用超级智能机器的世界的乐观态度。

“作为一项思想实验，想象一下只有一个人有一位超级聪明的律师，”扎克伯格写道。 “他将在法庭上拥有不公平的优势。 这将导致一个更糟糕的社会。 但现在想象一下每个人都有一位超级聪明的律师。 正义将会比现在更加公平和有效地得到执行。”

但扎克伯格对人工智能的乐观态度并不足以缓解华尔街对 Meta 第二季度财报的最初反应。 公布弱于预期的业绩后，该公司股价下跌近 8%。

根据彭博社的普遍预测，Meta 公布的每股收益为 6.18 美元，低于华尔街预期的 7.14 美元。 收入为 608 亿美元，超出分析师预测的 602.3 亿美元。

该公司还上调了今年预期费用和支出的下限。 Meta 首席财务官 Susan Li 表示，该公司第二季度“与法律诉讼相关的费用”为 24 亿美元，使总支出从 1620 亿美元增至 1690 亿美元，达到 1650 亿美元至 1690 亿美元。

预计 2026 年资本支出将从 1250 亿美元升至 1450 亿美元，从 1300 亿美元升至 1450 亿美元。 Meta 此前曾表示，其资本支出的很大一部分专门用于人工智能投资。

扎克伯格发起公关闪电战之际，投资者和分析师正在寻找该公司在人工智能基础设施上大规模支出的合理性，这一担忧导致该公司股价同比下跌 10%。

像 Meta 这样的大型科技公司，自由现金流的消耗越来越大，它们需要向消费者和华尔街推销人工智能的承诺，以捍卫他们的支出。 股市对扎克伯格在公司定于今晚晚些时候举行的财报电话会议上发表的言论的反应可能会揭示他的信息是否足以缓解投资者的担忧。

据彭博社本月报道，Meta 一直在努力打造一个能够与 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 竞争的人工智能模型，但它计划启动一项云业务来销售人工智能计算，从而将其巨额人工智能投资中的一些货币化。 该报告是今年为数不多的提振投资者信心的事情之一，刺激了该股长期下跌的势头。

财报发布前一天，扎克伯格在接受《纽约时报》和《金融时报》采访时，重申了他对人工智能去中心化和创造“个性化超级智能”时代的信念，每个人都拥有适合自己需求和信仰的人工智能助手。

尽管他没有具体说明 Meta 计划如何解决这个问题，但根据该公司的历史，个性化可能会要求消费者交出更多的数据。 尽管如此，扎克伯格表示，这比竞争对手的中心化模式更好。

扎克伯格对《纽约时报》表示：“我认为，不可能有一个仁慈的超级智能同时与所有人保持一致。”

咨询公司 Forrester Research 的副总裁兼研究总监 Mike Proulx 表示，Meta 可能“试图同时做太多事情”。

“Meta 的每一个主要增长通道现在都带来了信任损失，”普鲁克斯在列出 Meta 的新项目之前的一份声明中表示。 “人工智能生成的广告引发了新的品牌控制问题，智能眼镜带来了新的隐私问题，青少年安全仍然受到严格审查，员工追踪举措引发了数据收集方面的强烈反对。”

扎克伯格的叙述表明，Meta 需要将自己与竞争对手区分开来——他说，许多竞争对手正在发出充满关于人工智能未来的“厄运”的信息。

扎克伯格在《华尔街日报》上写道：“我不明白为什么那些相信人工智能将消除大多数工作和人类的大部分相关性的人会急于建设这样的未来。”

eMarketer 高级分析师 Minda Smiley 表示，尽管如此，Meta 围绕其人工智能系统创造积极信息的尝试可能会失败。

斯迈利在一份声明中表示：“扎克伯格希望围绕公司的人工智能雄心发出更具凝聚力的信息，这并不奇怪，尤其是在 Meta 试图开辟自己的道路之际。”

“但他所表现出的乐观、积极的语气与社交媒体公司因声称其伤害儿童并使儿童上瘾而引发的负面情绪形成鲜明对比。 这种并置可能会让 Meta 在一个已经落后的领域建立信誉变得更加困难。”

虽然扎克伯格为 Meta 的人工智能开发开源方法辩护，但该公司被迫对其之前开发产品的做法及其对用户产生的影响做出回应。

Meta 面临约 3,000 起诉讼，指控其故意制造致瘾产品，导致儿童受到伤害。 这些诉讼是由家庭、学区和州总检察长提起的。 四十二个州已在州法院起诉 Meta，田纳西州的案件目前正在审理中。 由 29 名总检察长提起的另一项联邦诉讼将于下个月在加利福尼亚州开庭审理。

“不断变化的监管环境也是一个主要的元风险，”普鲁克斯说。 “政策制定者更关注青少年福祉、成瘾和平台安全…… 青少年限制将影响 Meta 的覆盖范围。 对于一家依赖广告收入的公司来说，这是一个大问题。”

这些诉讼不仅对 Meta 的企业行为提出质疑，而且还对 Meta 的企业行为提出质疑。它们也付出了经济代价。 该公司已经遭受了破坏性损失，两个独立的陪审团认定 Meta 对伤害儿童负有责任，并判给原告数百万美元的赔偿金。 家庭、学校和立法者的律师表示，在 Meta 改变其产品设计之前，他们不会停止寻求高额赔偿。
